observations.text: SP, due to an unrehearsed lead change flow, did not act on the leader's visual signal at the point determined during the pre-flight briefing and did not assume formation leadership without uncertainty. Airspeed diverged 25 knots and altitude 350 feet from the briefed values during the exchange, beyond the code 1 tolerances. The IP had to direct the sequence and execute part of the handover. Further study of the Techniques and Procedures Manual lead change sequence is required.

SP, due to lack of communication of the recognised problem to the other cockpit, did not confirm the lead change command before manoeuvring and misinterpreted the exchange, with the result that neither A/C was navigating the formation. Exit heading was 15 degrees and altitude 400 feet from the briefed values, beyond the code 1 tolerances. The IP intervened and re-established the formation roles in flight.

SP performed the lead change within the desired standards for the Training Section, completing the handover after the IP's verbal prompts. Altitude reached 300 feet and airspeed 20 knots from the briefed values, at the code 1 limits, with the deviations recognised and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - reduced reliance on prompting and closer parameter control during the exchange are expected to improve.

SP acted on the leader's verbal signal without misinterpretation and assumed formation leadership after the command, complying with the B.O 3-1/ATC restrictions for lead change. Deviations of 200 feet in altitude and 15 knots in airspeed during the exchange were recognised and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the lead change at the point determined during the pre-flight briefing, without misinterpretation of the leader's signal, and assumed formation leadership immediately after receiving the command. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 6 knots and the exit heading within 3 degrees of the briefed values, with accuracy and speed and without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated the briefed lead change point and executed the handover exactly as briefed, with the leader's signal acknowledged and the formation roles unambiguous throughout. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 40 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and the exit heading within 1 degree, and the B.O 3-1/ATC restrictions were complied with at all times. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect power and pursuit technique while moving into the lead position, did not execute the lead change at the point determined during the pre-flight briefing and did not stabilise the formation on the briefed exit heading. Exit heading was 18 degrees and airspeed 30 knots from the briefed values, beyond the code 1 tolerances. The IP directed the correction and flew part of the reposition. Formation lead technique requires further ground preparation.

SP, due to failure to exercise formation lead responsibilities after the lead change, did not take up navigation and radio responsibility for the flight once leadership had been accepted. Altitude departed 380 feet from the briefed value and the formation was not manoeuvred for approximately one minute, beyond the code 1 tolerance. The IP assumed the lead and re-briefed the roles in flight.

SP, due to a late cross-check of the briefed lead change point against the navigation display, did not initiate the handover on time and completed it only after the IP's verbal instructions. Altitude reached 300 feet and airspeed 20 knots from the briefed values, at the code 1 limits, with the errors recognised and corrected with delay.

SP, due to an unstated request for a repeat of the instruction that was not understood, did not act on the leader's verbal signal and did not assume formation leadership without uncertainty. The exchange was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the exit heading 10 degrees and airspeed 20 knots from the briefed values, at the code 1 limits. Recognition and correction of the deviations were delayed.

SP performed the lead change at the briefed point and assumed formation leadership after receiving the command, within the desired standards for the Training Section. Deviations of 220 feet in altitude and 16 knots in airspeed occurred during the exchange and were recognised and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - closer parameter control through the handover is expected to improve.

SP executed the lead change without misinterpretation of the leader's signal and assumed formation leadership immediately, complying with the B.O 3-1/ATC restrictions for the exchange. Altitude was held within 120 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and the exit heading within 4 degrees of the briefed values, with accuracy and speed and without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the lead change at the exact point determined during the pre-flight briefing, with unambiguous acknowledgement of the leader's signal and immediate assumption of the formation lead. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and the exit heading within 2 degrees, and navigation and radio responsibilities were taken up without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incomplete visual scan of the leading A/C during the signal exchange, misinterpreted the lead change and manoeuvred while No1 was still leading the formation. Airspeed diverged 28 knots and altitude 420 feet from the briefed values, beyond the code 1 tolerances, and lateral separation was reduced. The IP took control to restore the formation geometry.

SP, due to lack of teamwork in the formation with no agreed division of lookout responsibility, did not confirm receipt of the lead change command and did not assume formation leadership after it was given. The flight drifted 350 feet in altitude and 12 degrees off the briefed exit heading, beyond the code 1 tolerances. The IP directed the sequence and executed part of the handover.

SP, due to a non-standardized lead change flow, did not execute the handover at the point determined during the pre-flight briefing and did not comply with the B.O 3-1/ATC restrictions for the exchange. The lead change was completed only after the IP's verbal instructions, with altitude 300 feet and the exit heading 10 degrees from the briefed values, at the code 1 limits. The errors were recognised and corrected with delay.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the formation's position relative to the briefed lead change point, did not initiate the exchange until prompted twice by the IP. Formation leadership was then assumed with uncertainty, with airspeed 20 knots and altitude 300 feet from the briefed values, at the code 1 limits. The deviations were recognised and corrected with delay.

SP, due to a late power reduction while moving into the lead position, did not hold the briefed airspeed through the exchange. Airspeed deviated 15 knots and altitude 200 feet from the briefed values, both recognised and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The lead change itself was executed at the briefed point and without misinterpretation of the leader's signal.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic during the exchange, did not hold the briefed exit heading immediately after assuming the formation lead. Exit heading deviated 8 degrees and altitude 180 feet from the briefed values, recognised and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Leadership was assumed after the command without uncertainty.

SP performed the lead change within the desired standards, executing it at the briefed point and assuming formation leadership after receiving the command. Altitude was held within 140 feet and airspeed within 9 knots of the briefed values, close to the upper edge of the desired band, and the exit heading required one correction to regain the briefed value. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter parameter control during the exchange is expected to improve.

SP executed the lead change at the point determined during the pre-flight briefing, without misinterpretation of the leader's signal, and assumed formation leadership immediately and unambiguously. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 40 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and the exit heading within 1 degree, and the B.O 3-1/ATC restrictions were complied with throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.
